property_summary: For any caller, when calling supplyTokenTo(amount, beneficiary) the reference contract credits the beneficiary's imBalances by the produced creditsIssued (i.e., imBalances(beneficiary) increases by creditsIssued); the mutant instead credits the caller, so there exist inputs where imBalances(beneficiary) in the mutant differs (not increased) versus the reference.

For any caller and beneficiary and any positive mAssetAmount, after supplyTokenTo(mAssetAmount, beneficiary) completes the reference credits imBalances(beneficiary) by the issued credits (i.e., imBalances(beneficiary) increases by the creditsIssued); the mutant instead credits imBalances(msg.sender), so there exist inputs where imBalances(beneficiary) in the mutant is not increased and thus differs from the reference.

For any caller and beneficiary and any positive mAssetAmount, after calling supplyTokenTo(mAssetAmount, beneficiary) the reference contract increases imBalances(beneficiary) by the credits issued (so imBalances(beneficiary) > 0 when creditsIssued>0), whereas the mutant credits the caller instead, so there exist inputs (caller != beneficiary and creditsIssued>0) where imBalances(beneficiary) remains unchanged and thus differs.

For any caller and beneficiary and any positive mAssetAmount that results in nonzero creditsIssued, the reference credits imBalances(beneficiary) by creditsIssued after supplyTokenTo; the mutant instead credits imBalances(msg.sender) so there exist inputs (caller != beneficiary and creditsIssued>0) where imBalances(beneficiary) does not increase and the property is violated.

For all callers, beneficiaries and positive mAssetAmount that produce nonzero credits, the reference contract increases imBalances(beneficiary) by the issued credits after supplyTokenTo; the mutant instead increases imBalances(msg.sender) so when caller != beneficiary and creditsIssued>0 the mutant violates this rule.

For any caller, amount and recipient, after a successful supplyTokenTo(mAssetAmount, to) the recipient's imBalances increases by exactly the creditsIssued returned from savings.depositSavings(mAssetAmount); the mutant erroneously adds an extra +1 causing imBalances[to] to be larger for some inputs.

For any caller, amount and recipient, calling supplyTokenTo(mAssetAmount, to) increases imBalances(to) by exactly the creditsIssued returned from savings.depositSavings(mAssetAmount); the mutant instead adds an extra +1 to imBalances[to], so there exist inputs where c.imBalances(to) differs by 1.

For any caller, amount and recipient, after calling supplyTokenTo(amount, to) the recipient's stored credits imBalances(to) increases exactly by the creditsIssued returned from savings.depositSavings(amount); the mutant instead increments by creditsIssued + 1, so there exist fuzzed inputs (recipient addresses and amounts) where imBalances differs by 1 and thus violates this invariant.

For any caller, amount and recipient, calling supplyTokenTo(mAssetAmount, to) increases imBalances(to) by exactly the creditsIssued returned from savings.depositSavings(mAssetAmount); the mutant adds an extra +1 to the stored imBalances, so there exist fuzzed inputs (amount and recipient) for which the public getter imBalances(recipient) differs (off by 1) compared to the correct rule.

For every call to supplyTokenTo(amount, to) where the caller has approved and the savings.depositSavings returns some creditsIssued, the stored imBalances(to) increases by exactly creditsIssued; the mutant erroneously adds an extra +1 to imBalances(to) for each call, so there exist fuzzed inputs (amount/to/caller) where the public getter imBalances(to) differs by 1 and thus violates this invariant.

For any caller (owner) the reference contract's approveMax sets the ERC20 allowance for the savings contract (savings address) to max for the underlying token; the mutant instead sets allowance to address(this) so reading the allowance for savings will differ — the reference always makes allowance(address(savings)) == type(uint256).max, which the mutant breaks for some inputs.
